1.explanation: The FileUploaderButton is part of the FileUploader component in the Carbon React library. According to the repository structure and naming conventions, the relevant code that contains the <label> for the uploader button is located in 'packages/react/src/components/FileUploader/FileUploader.js'. This is the file responsible for the UI of the FileUploader, including its button. Removing the invalid 'role' attribute from the label in this file will address the DAP accessibility violation. Other files (such as story or test files) use or test the component, but the bug is in the implementation file for the FileUploader component.
1.bug_scenario: The DAP violation warns 'Elements that use 'role' must reference a valid WAI-ARIA role.' The screenshot shows a <label role ... > element inside a file uploader button scenario. DAP flags this element because <label> should not use a generic 'role' unless it references a valid WAI-ARIA role. The fix is to remove the role from the label element in the FileUploaderButton UI component.

2.explanation: The file 'packages/react/src/components/FileUploader/FileUploader.js' is the most relevant to this bug. The FileUploaderButton is a part of the FileUploader component, so any issues related to how labels and roles are set for file upload buttons will be found here. To resolve the bug, the incorrect 'role' attribute from the <label> element within this component needs to be removed or corrected to comply with ARIA specifications and resolve the DAP violation. No configuration or auxiliary files are likely related to this markup/accessibility-specific bug.
2.bug_scenario: The bug scenario involves an accessibility violation detected by the DAP (Dynamic Assessment Plugin) on the React FileUploaderButton. The image and report highlight a DOM element (<label>) with a 'role' attribute that is not referencing a valid WAI-ARIA role, resulting in a DAP error. The issue is specifically triggered when using the FileUploaderButton, which is supposed to provide file upload functionality, but is currently causing an accessibility compliance failure due to misuse of the 'role' attribute.
